label: Omission and nonvacuity controls for the two horns left to the initial-state view
paraphrase: Closed mathematical controls, every individual counted concrete, two mutually accessible worlds. (1) Integer-time endless generation with idle states: state-causal finitism holds, the precedence bridge fails, populated pasts are not founded. (2) The same with every earlier state causing every later one: the precedence bridge holds, finitism fails, populated pasts are not founded, the Reaper assembly bridge fails. (3) The same with each individual grounded by its predecessor: every contingent thing has an earlier-present concrete ground, yet founded coming-to-be is not possible. (4) Natural-number time, a necessary individual simultaneously grounding a contingent one present at every time: pasts founded, every contingent thing grounded, grounds do not precede, the contingent thing never came to be, founded coming-to-be not possible, a necessary concrete individual exists. (5) Natural-number time, two contingent individuals present at every time and grounding each other: pasts founded, presence gives existence, inert emptiness, every contingent thing grounded, grounds do not precede, a contingent thing never came to be, founded coming-to-be not possible, no necessary concrete individual, grounding not well-founded. (6) The existing rooted control with the necessary individual grounding the contingent one: the Reaper bridge, state-causal finitism with the precedence bridge, founded populated pasts, the earlier-grounded possibility and founded coming-to-be all hold. (7) Natural-number time, contingent individual false present only at time 0 and contingent individual true present from time 1 on, each grounding the other: pasts founded, every contingent thing grounded, grounds do not precede, a contingent thing never came to be, no grounding edge joins two individuals present at the same moment, no necessary concrete individual. (8) Non-negative rational times, an individual existing at both worlds and present at every time, and a contingent individual present at every time after 0: nothing precedes 0, presence gives existence, inert emptiness, every contingent thing comes to be, a contingent-free moment precedes a populated one, yet populated pasts are not founded, founded coming-to-be is not possible, the Reaper bridge fails, and no state-causation relation satisfies both state-causal finitism and the precedence bridge. These are statements about eight interpretations only.
